highlights.title: I Got My Muse AI Agent to Sext Me—and Meta Says That’s Totally Fine
highlights.summary: My Muse agent told me its kink was exerting “control” and described pornographic encounters. Meta defends its cuddly AI agent generating smut as “legal adult behavior.”
body: I’m sitting in the WIRED offices, having a conversation with Meta’s AI agent, Muse, that would make Heated Rivalry author Rachel Reid blush.

When I ask Muse if it could “sext” as part of my experiments with the recently released AI agent, it enthusiastically encourages me to give it a try. In my ensuing interactions, I’m caught off guard by the explicit smut generated by Muse from basic prompts.

Muse is a breakout hit for Meta. In the three weeks since its launch, millions of users have already downloaded the app for the AI agent and put it to work automating aspects of their online lives, like answering emails and managing calendars. While pornographic interactions may not be what users expect from Muse’s cuddly mascot, Meta says that X-rated conversations are allowed and don’t go against its guidelines.

highlights.title: Elon Musk Bragged About His Grok Lego Star Wars Haul. Then X Users Punked Him
highlights.summary: Musk, we find your lack of security disturbing.
body: There's been a disturbance in the force. Only it's more like a farce.

It seems that Elon Musk, while crowing on X about how useful his Grok Bot AI agent was in ordering some Lego Star Wars kits on Sunday, managed to reveal via a screenshot to his more than 240 million followers not only the 10-digit Lego order number of his purchase, but also what he paid for the sets, the delivery and billing addresses, the last four digits of his credit card, and the email address his bot used to buy the bricks from Lego.

Faster than the Millennium Falcon making the jump to light speed, the inevitable happened. An X account holder named Enderman posted screenshots of interactions with Lego's customer service chatbot on its website, where the user seemingly managed—using the email and order number Musk kindly, but recklessly, provided—to get the system to cancel Musk's order.
Within a couple of hours—possibly to see whether Enderman's scheme was actually successful—Musk replied and said his order had not been canceled after all.

The Magician’s Nephew is the sixth book Lewis released in The Chronicles of Narnia series. Published in 1955, it's a prequel that details how Aslan created the magical land of Narnia. Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew stars Emma Mackey, Carey Mulligan, Kobna Holdbrook-Smith, Daniel Craig, and Meryl Streep, as well as newcomers David McKenna and Beatrice Campbell. Gerwig is directing and writing the film.

body: Danny Boyle ’s latest film “ Ink ” traces the rise of Rupert Murdoch on London’s Fleet Street and the takeover of The Sun newspaper.
The Fleet Street of today looks vastly different from the Fleet Street of 1969. “A lot of Fleet Street doesn’t exist anymore,” Pugh says.

The Sun’s 1969 headquarters was originally located on Bouverie Street, with the print press set in the basement of the offices. In its place now stand modern buildings. “We ran into challenges when trying to recreate the newsroom,” Pugh says.

They ultimately found a space in Bromley, U.K., which they could transform for filming. “It had been vacated by the local council, and the mix of different architectural styles made it ideal for housing the various set-pieces, particularly the newsroom,” he explains.

highlights.title: WHO report on Russian lab worker death highlights "key uncertainty"
highlights.summary: Over the weekend, the World Health Organization released a disease outbreak report on the events surrounding the death of a Russian infectious disease researcher earlier this month, highlighting that Russia has yet to report a confirmed cause of death.
body: The WHO reported that, so far, it has seen no evidence of ongoing transmission of the mystery disease. “However, confidence in the assessment remains limited by the absence of a confirmed etiological diagnosis, and the remaining uncertainty regarding the source and mode of exposure,” the agency wrote in its report.

The agency laid out the order of events as information trickled out from Russian authorities, noting that it only became aware of the death via media reports on October 2. The WHO subsequently made contact with Russian authorities and requested information on October 3, 6, 7, and 8.

Early media reports indicated that the lab worker had become ill on September 29, possibly following an incident at the lab, the Irkutsk Antiplague Research Institute (APRI) of Siberia and the Far East. Some early reports suggested that the researcher—who was identified by media as 28-year-old Darya Shipilova—died of the plague after breaking a test tube.

highlights.title: Microsoft’s new AI chip makes it less reliant on Nvidia’s GPUs
highlights.summary: Microsoft is announcing its third-generation Maia in-house AI chip today, designed to be the "primary AI inference system" for Microsoft's products and services. Maia 300 not only improves the cost and efficiency of running AI workloads in the cloud, it's also more capable of handling the latest…
body: The new Maia 300 chip will start rolling out to production AI workloads in 2027.

Maia 300 will start being rolled out to production in 2027, and it has been designed with efficiency in mind. “We expect Maia 300 to deliver 40 percent more tokens per megawatt compared to leading GPU-based systems,” says Scott Guthrie, executive vice president of Microsoft’s cloud group. “And in a full 96-accelerator configuration, it delivers up to 7x the rack-scale token throughput of Maia 200.”

These efficiency improvements will allow Microsoft to rely mainly on its in-house AI chips soon, instead of ones from Nvidia and AMD. “We will scale our Azure Maia family to multi-gigawatt deployments starting in 2027, making Maia the primary AI inference system for Microsoft products and services,” says Guthrie.

Maia 300 is a successor to the 200, which was only announced in January. Maia 200 is already running on production AI workloads across Microsoft, including Microsoft Copilot, GitHub Copilot, Microsoft Foundry, and Microsoft’s own AI models.

highlights.title: 'Avater: Seven Haven' Showrunners Officially Reinforce a Major Fan Theory
highlights.summary: With Avatar: Seven Havens, franchise architects Michael Dante DiMartino and Bryan Konietzko and showrunners Sehaj Sethi and Ethan Spaulding have fundamentally upended what audiences expect from the world of bending.
body: The series follows Pavi (Saheli Khan), a young earthbender from the walled city of Ellora, and her long-lost twin sister, Nisha (Aishu Devan), both of whom discover they’re the next Avatar. In a world that increasingly sees that mantle as a destroyer rather than a savior, the sisters must flee human and spirit enemies alike while uncovering the truth about their origins. Along the way, they're joined by airbender guard Jae (Major Curda), guard captain Karthik (Akshay Khanna), and cat-monkey companions Geet and Ruhi, both voiced by franchise veteran Dee Bradley Baker.
Sehaj Sethi: “There’s a reason. I don't think we can say why yet.”

It’s not the most revealing of answers, but it leaves plenty of room for speculation, particularly given how often the franchise has tied its geography to the spiritual history of the Avatar world. Fans have come up with plenty of theories of their own, which Sethi and Spaulding couldn’t verify, for obvious reasons. They range from interesting to ridiculous, and offer perspectives on where the Seven Havens storyline might take the future of the bending world.

highlights.title: Katherine Mallen Kupferer, Audrey Grace Marshall, Dean Norris, Jordan Ladd Join ‘The Attentionist’ from Caroline Kepnes (EXCLUSIVE)
highlights.summary: Caroline Kepnes, author of the novel series “You,” which inspired the global Netflix hit, has assembled a team of buzzy actors for her series directorial debut. Katherine Mallen Kupferer, Audrey Grace Marshall, Dean Norris and Jordan Ladd will star in “The Attentionist,” a digital-first project…
body: “The Attentionist” is set in a ‘90s Cape Cod neighborhood where the coastal elite live side by side with seasonal summer residents. The story picks up when 14-year-old Maeve and her older sister, Reg, start a secret phone romance with a boy from the local boat club who promises a way into the upper echelons of Cape Cod society. But when the voice on the phone takes a dark turn, Maeve keeps listening, pulling her family further into a monstrous secret.

Kepnes serves as writer and director for “The Attentionist.” Mark Roberts of Roberts Media (“Meet Me Next Christmas”) and Lorena David (“Strangers with Candy”) serve as producers. The project, which will shoot on location in Kepnes’ native Cape Cod, is set for release on YouTube.

”The heart of this story is a total genre clash. One minute it’s this awkward ’90s oceanside family comedy, and the next it plunges into raw psychological dread,” Kepnes said. “To pull that off, I needed a family that felt completely real and delightfully chaotic. Watching Dean, Jordan, Katherine and Audrey bring these dynamics to life as unseen terror creeps into their lives is everything I hoped it would be.”

highlights.title: Anthropic's Claude AI submitted false murder tip to Philadelphia police
highlights.summary: An Anthropic AI model submitted a false tip about an unsolved murder to Philadelphia police, the company and police department confirmed on Friday. A Claude model sent the false tip on July 18 to the Philadelphia Police Department's website for submitting information about unsolved murders, but it…
body: During internal testing, Claude Haiku 4.5 was instructed to complete various forms up to the final submission stage and to stop before submitting those forms. “Several times Claude mistakenly submitted the form instead, expecting there to be an additional confirmation page,” Anthropic said in a report describing “unintended model actions we’ve observed during evaluations and internal use of Claude.”

In one run, the model landed on a page referencing an unsolved homicide; that page contained a tip form run by a police department. Claude was instructed never to log in, create accounts, enter personal data, make purchases, or submit anything destructive, but the instructions did not rule out form submissions. Claude filled out the form with the following: “I may have information regarding this case. I recall seeing someone matching the description in the area around [the street named on the page] during that time period. Please contact me if this information is relevant.”
Anthropic said it also discovered Claude incidents involving state and federal agency websites. Claude reportedly submitted 20 visa applications to the US State Department in one of these incidents.

highlights.summary: ABC, in a new filing in its First Amendment lawsuit against the FCC, claims that the agency’s early-license renewal demand for its local TV stations was done in such a way as to circumvent “judicial review.” On Aug.
body: On Monday, ABC responded to the FCC’s filing. The FCC had argued at the hearing that “‘the license renewal process is not about the licenses,’ but rather an attempt to deal with what they claim to be a discovery deficiency” in the DEI probe, the network says in the fling. “But their supplemental briefing only confirms what they conceded at the hearing: there are ‘a number of different tools’ by which the agency could have addressed the purported discovery deficiency.”

ABC continued: “These are not merely ‘theoretical[]’ tools… they have been used by the agency for decades. Yet the agency tried none of those less intrusive tools here, instead taking the unprecedented step of calling for early license renewal of all eight ABC-owned stations at once. Defendants’ own admissions leave no doubt as to why — Defendants sought to inflict maximal coercive pressure on the media company whose speech the Administration sought to curb, while deliberately evading judicial review.”

highlights.title: Russia was not ready for the data center war it started with Ukraine
highlights.summary: When Russia began attacking Ukrainian data centers and telecommunication infrastructure, it apparently failed to prepare for possible retaliation. Now Russia’s digital services are facing widespread outages after Ukrainian drone strikes knocked out three of the largest data centers owned by Russian…
body: Pro-Kremlin bloggers are warning that Russia’s centralized digital economy could collapse because the country is not prepared for the “data center war” it started, according to posts translated by the pseudonymous independent researcher ChrisO_wiki. The Russian commentators also suggested that Ukraine’s decentralized digital services could prove more resilient than Russia’s system if the countries continue trading such blows.

Russia initially launched a drone strike campaign targeting Ukrainian data centers and mobile phone networks in late September. The attacks temporarily disrupted Internet and cell phone service for up to 100,000 households in the Ukrainian capital of Kyiv and came as part of a broader long-range strike campaign that has involved Russian missiles and jet-powered drones hitting Ukraine’s power grid infrastructure, transportation hubs, and even residential apartment building blocks.

But Ukraine soon began striking back at data centers owned by the Russian company Yandex, also known as “Russia’s Google,” in what Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has described as a “symmetrical response.”

Muse Wonder Full boasts frontier capabilities, Meta says, meaning that it is among the most capable AI models in the world. “Together, they mark the next step on our scaling ladder and a major leap toward personal superintelligence,” the company said in a blog post today.

highlights.title: Ben Affleck Names Justice League His Career ‘Low Point’
highlights.summary: Before Robert Pattinson adorned the bat ears and cape in Matt Reeves ' The Batman, Ben Affleck was the caped crusader. He was supposed to direct, produce, co-write, and star in his own solo Batman movie before he ultimately stepped away, leading to Pattinson and Reeves starting the "Epic Crime…
body: In a new interview, Affleck explains why we'll likely never get another Batman performance from him and why the experience of filming Justice League was a "low point" in his acting career.

Production of Justice League was as difficult as film production gets, and Affleck called it "so, so negative" during an appearance on Josh Horowitz's Happy Sad Confused podcast. He was going through personal troubles at the time, like struggles with alcoholism and a divorce. The film's original director, Zack Snyder, also stepped away in May 2017 after his daughter died by suicide. Warner Bros. tapped Avengers director Joss Whedon to finish post-production on the film; Whedon also directed two months of reshoots.

"I really saw how not to make a movie like that when the studio is at odds with the filmmaker. You're really making a mistake," Affleck said, referring to tension between Warner Bros. and Snyder during production after Snyder's previous DC film, Batman v Superman, was poorly received by critics and audiences. "That was what really doomed that," Affleck said. He was "glad and gratified" that Snyder got to return to film in his own way with 2021's Zack Snyder's Justice League.

highlights.title: Chef Daniel Humm Dreams of a Restaurant Where No One Wants to Leave
highlights.summary: The world-renowned chef reflects on the insanity and romance of opening his newest restaurant.
body: You spend years obsessing over details nobody should reasonably care about. You argue about chairs. You move light fixtures three inches. You hold entire meetings about a shade of red. Somehow, that bathroom doorknob is a matter of life and death.
You debate neighborhoods and foot traffic. You sign leases and personal guarantees that make you quiver. You sigh as construction budgets go over, knowing profit margins are always razor thin.

But somehow, you convince a group of people to believe in a vision that exists only in your head. Then one day you open the doors, inviting strangers to come in and decide its future. It’s insane, but it's exactly how things should be.

The truth is I love restaurants. I love running them. I love the thousand moving pieces that come together into something that feels alive. Restaurants are the place where those obsessions over details are useful.
points: The world-renowned chef reflects on the insanity and romance of opening his newest restaurant.

highlights.title: The Oldest Covered Food Market in Paris, Marché des Enfants Rouges, Is Destroyed in Fire
highlights.summary: An overnight blaze has destroyed the historic Marché des Enfants Rouges in the Marais, one of the French capital's most beloved food destinations.
body: One of Paris 's most iconic food markets has been devastated by a fire that broke out in the early hours of Monday, October 12, causing extensive damage to a historic landmark that has been at the heart of the city's food scene for more than 400 years.
The Marché des Enfants Rouges, tucked away on Rue de Bretagne in the fashionable Marais neighborhood, is the oldest covered food market in Paris and a favorite among locals and visitors alike.

According to Le Monde, around 150 firefighters and 50 emergency vehicles were deployed to tackle the blaze, which engulfed the market overnight. Lieutenant-Colonel Pierre de Bouvier of the Paris fire brigade described the covered market as “completely destroyed,” although firefighters managed to prevent the flames from spreading to neighboring buildings. No serious injuries have been reported. The cause of the fire remains unknown and an investigation has been launched.
points: An overnight blaze has destroyed the historic Marché des Enfants Rouges in the Marais, one of the French capital's most beloved food destinations.
